h1: Frozen shoulder treatment in Kukatpally, Hyderabad, without surgery
summary: Frozen shoulder (adhesive capsulitis) is a painful stiffening of the shoulder joint, most common between about 40 and 60 and in people with diabetes. At Halcyon in Kukatpally, Hyderabad, the shoulder is examined and scanned with ultrasound in the same appointment, and frozen shoulder is treated without surgery — with a suprascapular nerve block to ease the pain and hydrodilatation to stretch the tightened capsule — alongside a movement programme. Procedures are done under local anaesthetic, as day care.

quick_facts.label: Hospital stay
quick_facts.value: Day care, home the same day

paragraphs: In frozen shoulder the capsule — the lining that surrounds the shoulder joint — becomes inflamed, then thickens and tightens. As it contracts, the shoulder loses movement in every direction, and it hurts, often worst at night.

It usually passes through three overlapping stages: a painful “freezing” stage, a stiff “frozen” stage where pain eases but movement stays poor, and a slow “thawing” stage. Left alone it can take a long time to settle, which is why treatment aims to ease the pain and get the shoulder moving sooner.
It can follow an injury or a period of keeping the arm still, but often starts without an obvious cause. It is more likely in:
bullets: People with diabetes or thyroid problems
After a fracture, surgery or a spell with the arm in a sling
Women slightly more often than men
A deep ache in the shoulder that is worse at night and lying on that side
Stiffness that keeps getting worse over weeks
Difficulty reaching overhead, behind your back or combing your hair
Movement lost in every direction, not just one
The other shoulder sometimes affected later

sections.h2: How Halcyon confirms it is frozen shoulder
paragraphs: Several shoulder problems cause pain and stiffness, so the cause is checked first. At Halcyon’s Kukatpally centre the consultant examines how the shoulder moves — both when you move it and when it is moved for you — and scans it with diagnostic ultrasound in the same room.
The scan helps tell frozen shoulder apart from a rotator cuff tear, bursitis or arthritis, and the neck is checked if it may be contributing. Bring any X-ray or MRI reports you already have.

Whichever is used, it runs alongside a movement programme, because keeping the shoulder moving is what holds on to the range that has been freed up.
bullets: Suprascapular nerve block — quietens the main nerve supplying the shoulder joint, easing pain so you can move and exercise it
Hydrodilatation — fluid placed into the joint under guidance to stretch the tightened capsule

sections.h2: What to expect on the day and after
paragraphs: If a procedure is right for you, it is usually done in the same appointment, under local anaesthetic and ultrasound guidance. You stay awake throughout, there is no general anaesthetic and no admission, and most people are home within about two hours.

You leave with aftercare instructions, the exercises to start and a review date. How quickly the shoulder improves varies with the stage and how long it has been stiff, and the consultant gives you a realistic answer for yours.
Book an assessment if shoulder pain and stiffness have lasted more than a few weeks, disturb your sleep or keep getting worse. Seek urgent care at a hospital emergency department instead for:
bullets: Sudden left shoulder or arm pain with chest pain, breathlessness or sweating, which can be a heart problem
A fall or injury after which the shoulder looks deformed or you cannot move the arm
A hot, swollen, very painful shoulder with fever

faqs.q: Can frozen shoulder be treated without surgery?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. At Halcyon, frozen shoulder is treated with a suprascapular nerve block to ease the pain and hydrodilatation to stretch the tightened joint capsule, done under local anaesthetic as day care in Kukatpally, Hyderabad. It is run alongside a movement programme, because keeping the shoulder moving is what holds on to the range that has been freed up.

faqs.q: How long does frozen shoulder last?
faqs.a: Without treatment, frozen shoulder can take many months to settle on its own as it moves through the painful, stiff and thawing stages. Treatment aims to ease the pain sooner and help you regain movement. How long yours takes depends on the stage and how long the shoulder has been stiff, and the consultant will give you a realistic idea after examining and scanning it.

faqs.q: What is hydrodilatation for frozen shoulder?
faqs.a: Hydrodilatation is a procedure in which fluid is placed into the shoulder joint under guidance to stretch a capsule that has tightened. It is done under local anaesthetic, and it is usually followed by a movement programme so that the gain in range is kept rather than lost again.

faqs.q: Is frozen shoulder more common with diabetes?
faqs.a: Yes. Frozen shoulder is noticeably more common in people with diabetes, and it can be more stubborn in them. If you have diabetes and your shoulder is becoming painful and stiff, it is worth having it assessed early.

faqs.q: Will I be awake during the procedure?
faqs.a: Yes. Frozen shoulder procedures at Halcyon are done under local anaesthetic with ultrasound guidance, so you stay awake and talking throughout. There is no general anaesthetic and no hospital admission. Most people are home within about two hours, with aftercare instructions, exercises and a review date.

symptoms: Loss of range of movement in all directions
Difficulty reaching overhead or behind the back
causes: Inflammation and thickening of the shoulder joint capsule
